subject: ByteFront: coordinated incident update & customer commitments
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: ALERT: ByteFront reports 503s, automatic failover not triggered

Hi Camila —

On-call noticed a spike of 503 responses for ByteFront's production inference pool at 08:58 UTC. Automatic failover did not trigger for a subset of requests hitting the reserved cluster. We're into an incident call now (Zoom link below). Marcus and Evelyn are on the bridge to triage root cause; I wanted to loop you in early since this impacts ByteFront's peak batch window.

Immediate notes:
- Error pattern: 503 + "kv cache pressure" in logs from 08:58–09:06 UTC
- Affected footprint: 18% of ByteFront traffic (routing by token hash)
- Current mitigation: temporary routing to a warm fallback model (in progress)

Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210
PagerDuty: INC-4591

Ben
Senior On‑Call Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@bytefront.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -0000
Subject: RE: ByteFront: immediate update — our actions and what to expect next

Raj —

Thank you for the flag this morning and for being patient while our team pulled the bridge together. Quick executive summary for ByteFront customers:

What happened: a subset of inference requests experienced transient 503 errors due to unexpected KV cache pressure during a traffic spike. This prevented our automatic failover from covering 100% of impacted traffic immediately.

What we did (first 30 minutes):
- Diverted traffic away from the affected allocation to a warm fallback model to restore successful responses for the bulk of requests.
- Applied a tuned cache eviction policy to reduce pressure on the afflicted instances.
- Raised priority to SEV-1 internal status and mobilized the on-call + runtime team.

Status now (09:45 UTC):
- ~95% of traffic is restored to normal; a small fraction (approx 2–4% of requests) may still see elevated latency for a short window while we complete validation.
- We have a bridge running and Marcus is leading the root cause investigation.

Customer commitments we are making today:
1) Immediate restore and verification — our engineering team will keep the bridge open until traffic is confirmed stable across all ByteFront routes.
2) Post-incident technical report — a short postmortem delivered within 48 hours that includes timeline, root cause, and concrete remediation steps.
3) Credits — if you saw impact to availability beyond the window we define in the report, we'll follow Redwood's SLA credit process; we will propose credits in the postmortem.
4) Preventive change — we will stage and test an automatic fallback policy update to ensure failover coverage for similar cache-pressure patterns.

I will keep you updated every hour from the bridge and will share the postmortem draft within the 48-hour window. If you'd like the COO or Head of Customer Reliability to join a call later today, say the word and I will escalate.

Best,

Camila Reyes
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555‑0192
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@bytefront.io>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: support@bytefront.io
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: RE: ByteFront: immediate update — our actions and what to expect next

Camila —

Appreciate the clear summary and the fast response. We saw the errors in our dashboards from 08:55–09:06 UTC and some downstream worker queues backed up briefly. The warm fallback helped; we logged about 20 failing jobs that retried successfully.

Two asks from our side:
- Please include the exact request ids (we can share a sample) in the postmortem so we can cross-check with our logs.
- If you end up proposing an SLA credit, can you include an approximate amount in the draft so our finance team has context for approvals?

I'm available to jump on the bridge if useful — otherwise please feel free to send the hourly notes.

Thanks,
Raj
Head of Platform Engineering
ByteFront
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -0000
Subject: INTERNAL: action items from bridge — next 24h checklist

Team —

Recap from the bridge: KV cache pressure + a race in eviction and routing selection prevented automatic fallback for a minority of requests. Marcus outlined suspected sequence; Evelyn will confirm with memory-profiles and telemetry. Ben will collate bridgelog and sample request ids for ByteFront.

Immediate action items (owners):
- Ben: export bridgelog-20260714.txt and include sample request ids that Raj asked for (ETA: 12:00 UTC).
- Marcus: reproduce the eviction sequence in staging and test the proposed automatic fallback config (ETA: 18:00 UTC).
- Evelyn: collect memory and kernel traces for the affected hosts and upload to the postmortem doc (ETA: 15:00 UTC).
- Camila: prepare a customer-facing one-pager with timeline and tentative credits (ETA: 17:00 UTC).

We will maintain the bridge through the afternoon and plan a short exec-sync at 16:00 UTC to finalize the 48h postmortem outline. Please add any blockers to the bridge chat.

Camila
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@bytefront.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 13:38:00 -0000
Subject: FOLLOW-UP: confirmed restores, deliverables and 48h next steps

Raj —

Quick follow-up from the bridge closure at 13:20 UTC: all ByteFront routes are verified stable. Attached are the bridgelog excerpt and our proposed customer commitments PDF. Highlights:

- Restoration: verified at 13:10 UTC across all regions; no new 503s in the last 40 minutes.
- Evidence: bridgelog-20260714.txt (attached) contains sample request ids and error traces you requested.
- Deliverables timeline:
  • Bridgelog and sample ids — delivered (attached)
  • 48-hour postmortem draft — expected by 09:00 UTC on 2026-07-16
  • Proposed SLA credit estimate — included in attached PDF (draft; we'll finalize in postmortem)
  • Preventive config rollout plan — Marcus will present the rollout plan and staging test results in the postmortem.

Attachments: bridgelog-20260714.txt (text), customer-commitments-20260714.pdf (draft)

If you'd like a short wrap call with my manager (Evelyn) and Marcus to walk through the technical mitigation, we can schedule for tomorrow at your convenience.

Thanks again for working with us through the event. We'll follow through on the 48-hour commitment and include any further credit adjustments if the finalized window requires it.

Best,

Camila Reyes
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
